proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated $R$-subalgebras $R_i\subseteq V$, ordered by inclusion, and write $F_i=\operatorname{Frac}R_i\subseteq L$. This set contains $R$ and is directed: adjoining the union of two finite generating sets gives an upper bound. Every $v\in V$ belongs to $R[v]$, so $\varinjlim_iR_i=V$. Every $\lambda\in L$ has the form $v/w$ for $v,w\in V$, $w\ne0$, and both lie in some $R_i$; hence $\varinjlim_iF_i=L$. These are colimits as rings because the systems consist of inclusions and their unions have the asserted elements. The affine-limit theorem gives $\operatorname{Spec}V=\varprojlim_i\operatorname{Spec}R_i$. Each base scheme is qcqs by the affine-scheme lemma; transitions are affine: over an affine open $U$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, the affine fibre-product formula makes its inverse image $\operatorname{Spec}(R_k\otimes_{R_i}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U))$ for $k\ge i$.

source.place: Tags 01YW and 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit and lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit); directed family of subalgebras constructed explicitly

proof.text: Apply finitely presented algebra descent to the given finitely presented $V$-algebra $B$. Obtain $a\in I$, a finitely presented $R_a$-algebra $C_a$, and a chosen $V$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha_a:C_a\otimes_{R_a}V\simeq B$. For every $i\ge a$ put $C_i=C_a\otimes_{R_a}R_i$ and $A_i=A\otimes_RR_i$. Both are finitely presented over $R_i$ by finite-presentation base change. Tensor associativity identifies their further base changes with $B$ via $\alpha_a$ and with $A_V$, respectively; on pure tensors this sends $(c\otimes r)\otimes v$ to $c\otimes rv$.

Transfer the given structure map $u:A_V\to B$ along $\alpha_a$ to a map $A_a\otimes_{R_a}V\to C_a\otimes_{R_a}V$. Apply map descent, clause (2) of the cited node, to these two finitely presented $R_a$-algebras and the directed upper tail of $a$. After increasing $a$ there is an $R_a$-algebra map $u_a:A_a\to C_a$ whose base change is this transferred map. Let $u_i=u_a\otimes_{R_a}R_i$ for all $i\ge a$. Consequently each $\alpha_i:C_i\otimes_{R_i}V\simeq B$ is an isomorphism of $A_V$-algebras for the structure $u_i$, not merely of $V$-algebras.

The map $u_a$ is of finite presentation. Indeed, choose presentations $A_a=R_a[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ and $C_a=R_a[y_1,\ldots,y_t]/(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, and represent $u_a(x_j)$ by $h_j(y)$. Then
$$C_a\simeq A_a[y_1,\ldots,y_t]/(g_1,\ldots,g_s,\ x_1-h_1(y),\ldots,x_n-h_n(y)).$$
To verify the formula, substitute $x_j=h_j(y)$; the extra relations $f_k(h(y))$ already belong to $(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$ because $u_a$ is a well-defined map. The two substitutions are inverse. This is a finite presentation, and the same formula holds after replacing $R_a$ by any $R_i$. In particular $C_a$ is of finite type over $A_a$.

source.place: Definition Tag 00F3 (definition-finite-type); explicit finite relative presentation

proof.text: Apply finite-map descent with base system $R_i$, initial algebras $A_a,C_a$, and map $u_a$. The limit map is the given finite $A_V\to B$, and $C_a$ is of finite type over $A_a$ by step 4, so every hypothesis of the cited node holds. It yields $b\ge a$ such that $C_b$ is finite as an $A_b$-module. This remains true for every $i\ge b$: if $c_1,\ldots,c_N$ generate $C_b$ over $A_b$, their tensors generate $C_b\otimes_{R_b}R_i$ over $A_b\otimes_{R_b}R_i$, by expanding a pure tensor and then a finite sum of pure tensors. No injectivity of any map into $B$ is asserted or needed.

Apply flat-map descent to the same base system on its upper tail, now with initial algebras $R_b$ and $C_b$ and the structure map $R_b\to C_b$. This map is finitely presented by step 2; its limit is $V\to B$, which is flat by hypothesis. The cited node therefore gives $c\ge b$ such that $C_i$ is flat over $R_i$ for every $i\ge c$. All finite-presentation statements from steps 2 and 4 and finiteness from step 5 continue to hold on this upper tail.

source.place: Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat), part (3), with module equal to the algebra itself

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $V$, apply the affine algebraic-closure criterion to $B\otimes_V\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Its tensor product with an algebraic closure of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is reduced by the hypothesis on all maps from $V$ to algebraically closed fields. Thus every fibre ring is geometrically reduced. Let $E\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R_c$ be the geometric-reducedness locus of $C_c/R_c$. The cited fibre-locus node says both that $E$ is constructible and that its inverse image under every base change is the corresponding locus. Its inverse image in $\operatorname{Spec}V$ is therefore the whole spectrum. Apply the constructible-containment lemma to the affine inverse system of step 1 to find $d\ge c$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ maps into $E$ for every $i\ge d$. By the same base-change formula every fibre of $C_i/R_i$ is geometrically reduced. A map $R_i\to\Omega$ to an algebraically closed field factors through the residue field at its kernel; hence $C_i\otimes_{R_i}\Omega$ is reduced. This argument also covers empty fibres.

source.place: Tags 0579 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible) and 0576 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced); limits.tex Tag 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible); varieties.tex Tag 035X

proof.text: Set $\bar A_i=A_i\otimes_{R_i}F_i$, $\bar C_i=C_i\otimes_{R_i}F_i$ for $i\ge d$. These are finitely presented $F_i$-algebras by finite-presentation base change. Since $\varinjlim_iF_i=L$, their limit map is precisely the given generic isomorphism $u_L:A\otimes_RL\to B\otimes_VL$, using $\alpha_d$. Apply clause (2) of map descent over the field system $F_i$ to its specified inverse $u_L^{-1}$. At some $e\ge d$ it gives $v_e:\bar C_e\to\bar A_e$ with base change $u_L^{-1}$. The composites $v_eu_e$ and $u_ev_e$ become the respective identity maps over $L$. Apply clause (3) twice, then choose a common upper bound $j\ge e$, so both composites equal the identities over $F_j$. Thus the map $A_j\otimes_{R_j}F_j\to C_j\otimes_{R_j}F_j$ is an isomorphism, and its base change to $L$ is the specified $u_L$. All properties obtained on the upper tail $i\ge d$ remain valid at $j$.

source.place: Tag 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras), parts (2) and (3), applied to the fraction-field system; Tag 05G5 for finite-presentation base change

proof.text: Put $R'=R_j$, $B'=C_j$, and $F'=F_j$. If $R'=R[r_1,\ldots,r_N]$, its fraction field inside $L$ equals $F(r_1,\ldots,r_N)$: this field contains $R'$ and inverses of its nonzero elements, and conversely its generators belong to $\operatorname{Frac}R'$. Apply the cited finite-subextension lemma to $L/F$ with the empty transcendence basis and the elements $r_1,\ldots,r_N$. The empty family is algebraically independent, and its generated field is $F$ over which $L$ is algebraic, so it is a transcendence basis. The finite subset of that empty index set must be empty. The conclusion gives that $F'=F(r_1,\ldots,r_N)$ is finite separable over $F$, including $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness), proof, finite-subextension assertion, specialized to an empty transcendence basis

proof.text: The inclusion $R\subseteq R'\subseteq V$ gives the required factorization of spectra. The source is integral, with generic point $(0)$ and function field $F\prime$, by clause (2) of the spectrum-of-a-domain lemma applied to the subring $R\prime\subseteq L$. The morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is separated by the affine-source lemma. It is of finite type: for any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, the affine fibre-product formula identifies its preimage with $\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_RD)$. This algebra is generated over $D$ by the finite list $r_1\otimes1,\ldots,r_N\otimes1$, and its spectrum is quasi-compact by the affine-qcqs lemma. This verifies both clauses in the finite-type definition on every affine open of the target. Its generic point maps to $(0)$ and its function-field extension is $F'/F$, finite separable by step 9. These are exactly Temkin's integral-source, separated finite-type quasi-alteration conditions. The isomorphism $\alpha_j:B'\otimes_{R'}V\simeq B$ from step 3 is $A_V$-linear, and step 8 verifies its compatibility with the specified generic identification. Steps 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 give all remaining clauses for $B'$.

title: Spreading finite generic modifications from a valuation subring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative domain, $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$, and let $L/F$ be a separable algebraic extension. Let $V\subseteq L$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $L$, with $R\subseteq V$. A valuation ring means that $x\in V$ or $x^{-1}\in V$ for each $x\in L^\times$. Let $A$ be a flat finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and put $A_V=A\otimes_R V$. Suppose $B$ is a commutative $A_V$-algebra finite as an $A_V$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], flat and finitely presented over $V$, such that the given map $A_V\otimes_V L\to B\otimes_V L$ is an isomorphism and $B\otimes_V\Omega$ is reduced for every map $V\to\Omega$ to an algebraically closed field. Then there are a finitely generated $R$-subalgebra $R'\subseteq V$ and a commutative $A'=A\otimes_R R'$-algebra $B'$ such that $F'=\operatorname{Frac}R'$ is finite separable over $F$, $B'$ is finite and finitely presented as an $A'$-algebra, $B'$ is flat and finitely presented over $R'$, and $B'\otimes_{R'}\Omega$ is reduced for every map $R'\to\Omega$ to an algebraically closed field. The given map $A'\otimes_{R'}F'\to B'\otimes_{R'}F'$ is an isomorphism. There is an isomorphism $B'\otimes_{R'}V\simeq B$ of $A_V$-algebras inducing the specified generic identification. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is an integral separated finite-type quasi-alteration through which $\operatorname{Spec}V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ factors; finite type and separated have the meanings of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [def-weil-proper-morphism].
